{{Infobox company |name=100 Thieves |location=United States |image=100 Thieves full lightmode.png |imagedark=100 Thieves full darkmode.png |website=https://www.100thieves.com/ |instagram=100thieves |twitter=100Thieves |facebook=100Thieves |youtube=100thieves |reddit=100thieves |foundeddate=2016-04-18 }} '''100 Thieves''' (often abbreviated with '''100T''') is a professional esports organization and lifestyle brand founded by former Call of Duty professional [[:callofduty:Nadeshot|Nadeshot]] in 2016. {{GameArticle}} ==Competitive History== The organization made their debut at MLG Anaheim Open 2016 in April 2016, with a roster featuring a then former world champion in [[callofduty:ACHES|ACHES]]. The roster was released in July of that year, which resulted in a temporary hiatus for the organization's esports ambitions.{{cite web|url=https://www.thescoreesports.com/news/8943|title=Hundred Thieves release their roster|date=2016-07-08|publisher=[[theScore Esports]]}} ''100 Thieves'' returned to esports with the announcement of a [[leagueoflegends:100_Thieves|League of Legends franchise slot]].{{cite web|url=http://www.lolesports.com/en_US/teams|title=A NEW ERA BEGINS|author=''LoL Esports''|date=2017-11-20|publisher=[http://www.lolesports.com/en_US ''LoL Esports'']|language={{Flag|usuk}} English}} Since then, the organization has branched out to [[valorant:100 Thieves|Valorant]], [[fortnite:100 Thieves|Fortnite]] and has had a short stint in [[counterstrike:100 Thieves|Counter-Strike]]. Upon the announcement of the [[leagueoflegends:LoL_Championship_of_The_Americas|LTA]], it was revealed that 100 Thieves sold their League of Legends franchise slot, becoming a guest team, leading to their eventual exit after the 2025 season.{{cite web |url=https://twitter.com/LCSOfficial/status/1852032798107779405|title=The future of League of Legends Esports in the Americas. Welcome to the LTA.|author=[[LCS]]|publisher=Twitter|date=2024-10-31}}{{cite web|url=https://x.com/100Thieves/status/1946314093234938101|title=The final chapter of an eight-year heist|author=[[100 Thieves]]|date=2025-07-18}} {{See also |leagueoflegends:100 Thieves/History|l1=History of 100T LoL Team }} ===Game Timeline=== {{TeamTimeline |height=400|startYear=2016 |game1=callofduty |game1start=2016-04-18|game1end=2016-07-02|game1start2=2018-08-28|game1end2=2019-10-24|game1start3=2020-11-07 |game2=leagueoflegends |game2start=2017-11-20|game2end=2025-11-18 |game3=counterstrike |game3start=2017-12-12|game3end=2018-01-31|game3start2=2019-10-31|game3end2=2020-10-18|game3start3=2025-11-13 |game4=fortnite |game4start=2018-06-09|game4end=2022-08-17 |game5=apexlegends |game5start=2019-02-25|game5end=2020-05-28|game5start2=2021-10-08|game5end2=2023-09-22|game5start3=2024-11-11|game5end3=2026-01-07 |game6=valorant |game6start=2020-06-04 |game7=marvelrivals |game7start=2025-03-13|game7end=2025-11-17|game7start2=2026-02-10 |game8=streetfighter |game8start=2025-05-14|game8end=2025-09-14 |game9=teamfighttactics|game9start=2025-05-15|game9end=2025-12-31 |game10=rainbowsix |game10start=2026-03-09 }} ==Corporate History== Matthew "[[callofduty:Nadeshot|Nadeshot]]" Haag announced the launch of his esports organization on April 18th, 2016, naming it '''100 Thieves''' and signing a Call of Duty team.{{cite web|url=https://dotesports.com/call-of-duty/news/nadeshot-launches-100thieves-organization-10010|title=Nadeshot Launches 100Thieves Organization|date=2016-04-18|author=[[Grey Hester]]|publisher=[[Dot Esports]]}} After dissappointing results, the company released the roster just 3 months later, in July, commencing a hiatus in esports activities for the organization. That same month, the organization announced their first limited edition apparel drop, which saw the brand turn into an apparel company for the time being. {{citation needed}} It would take until November 2017 for the organization to return into esports. On the 20th of that month, the organization announced its entrance into League of Legends by acquiring a spot in the [[leagueoflegends:LCS|LCS]], thanks to financial backing from [[wikipedia:Dan Gilbert|Dan Gilbert]], the owner of the [[wikipedia:Cleveland Cavaliers|Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|url=https://dotesports.com/league-of-legends/news/nadeshot-100-thieves-na-lcs-franchise-slot-18867|title=Nadeshot on 100 Thieves’ acceptance into the NA LCS: “We’re gonna be hyper-focused on esports, content creation, and apparel”|date=2017-11-20|author=[[Aaron Mickunas]]|publisher=[[Dot Esports]]}} The following year saw 100 Thieves expand its esports operations aggressively, from returning to Call of Duty to entering the Fortnite scene.{{cite web|url=https://thegamehaus.com/call-of-duty/nadeshot-100-thieves-cod-return/2018/08/30/|title=Nadeshot’s 100 Thieves announce Call of Duty return|date=2018-08-30|author=[[Arran Francis]]|publisher=[[The Game Haus]]}}{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/100Thieves/status/1005538879523287040|title=100 THIEVES FORTNITE ANNOUNCEMENT|date=2018-06-09|publisher='''100 Thieves'''}} On October 23rd, 2018, 100 Thieves announced that it had completed a Series A funding round co-led by [[wikipedia:Scooter Braun|Scooter Braun]] and [[wikipedia:Drake|Drake]].{{cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/mattperez/2018/10/23/drake-and-scooter-braun-invest-in-esports-company-100-thieves/?sh=6efe209710a9|title=Drake And Scooter Braun Invest In Esports Company 100 Thieves|date=2018-10-23|author=[[Matt Perez]]|publisher=[[Forbes]]}} In July 2019, the company announced it had completed another funding round, garnering $35 million.{{cite web|url=https://nypost.com/2019/07/16/drakes-esports-team-100-thieves-raises-35-million/|title=Drake’s esports team 100 Thieves raises $35 million|date=2019-07-16|author=[[Josh Kosman]]|publisher=[[New York Post]]}} On November 6th, 2020, 100 Thieves announced that it had acquired a [[callofduty:Call_of_Duty_League|Call of Duty League]] slot from [[Immortals]], branding the team as [[:callofduty:Los Angeles Thieves|Los Angeles Thieves]].{{cite web|url=https://esportsobserver.com/100-thieves-cdl-slot-igc/|title=100 Thieves Buys Call of Duty League Slot From Immortals Gaming Club, Reveals L.A. web|url=https://www.reddit.com/r/100thieves/comments/4krcyk/100_thieves_beginning_till_now/|title=100 Thieves: Beginning Till '''100 Thieves''', stating that he wanted to return home to Michigan.{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/NICKMERCS/status/1131942975410458625|title=Moving forward|date=2019-05-24|author='''NICKMERCS'''|publisher=Twitter|language={{Flag|usuk}} English}} Days later, he revealed on a livestream that [[:callofduty:Nadeshot|Nadeshot]] broke certain promises: "when you give me your word and you promise certain things to me as a friend and a business partner and I put years of time into a thing we basically started and then everything changes, and I don’t get what I was promised, I’m gonna have problems with it."{{cite web|url=https://www.dexerto.com/entertainment/nickmercs-explains-why-he-wants-nothing-to-do-with-nadeshot-after-100-thieves-exit-659267/|title=NICKMERCS explains why he wants “nothing to do with Nadeshot” after 100 Thieves exit|date=2019-05-25|author=''Dexerto''|publisher=''Dexerto''|language={{Flag|usuk}} English}} Matthew Haag has not spoken about the issue, though the situation came web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/christinasettimi/2020/12/05/the-most-valuable-esports-companies-2020/?sh=78553ad273d0|title=The Most Valuable Esports Companies 2020|author=[[Christina Settimi]]|date=2020-12-05}} {{GameArticle}} ==History== ===Competitive History=== Gen.G Esports' start came with the acquisition of an [[overwatch:Overwatch_League|Overwatch League]] franchise spot, naming the team the [[:overwatch:Seoul Dynasty|Seoul Dynasty]]. {{cite web|url=https://esports-marketing-blog.com/seoul-team-overwatch-league-announces-official-name-seoul-dynasty/|title=The Seoul Team of the Overwatch League Announces its Official Name, ‘Seoul Dynasty’|date=2017-10-26|author=|publisher=[[Esports Marketing Blog]]}} In the leadup to this announcement, KSV eSports acquired the roster of [[overwatch:Lunatic-Hai|Lunatic-Hai]], on August 21st, 2017. {{cite web|url=https://www.thescoreesports.com/news/14949|title=KSV signs Lunatic-Hai players to play for Seoul Overwatch League team|date=2017-08-22|author=[[Daniel Rosen]]|publisher=[[The Score Esports]]}} On October 24th, 2017, it was announced that KSV acquired the rosters of two South Korean Heroes of the Storm (HOTS) teams - [[heroes:MVP Black|MVP Black]] and [[heroes:MVP Miracle|MVP Miracle]], both considered leading teams in the title. {{cite web|url= https://esportsinsider.com/2017/10/ksv-acquires-top-hots-teams-mvp-black-mvp-miracle/|title=KSV acquires top HotS teams MVP Black and MVP Miracle|date=2017-10-24|author=[[Sam Cooke]]|publisher=[[EsportsInsider]]}} On November 28th, KSV announced it had to drop the now [[heroes:KSV Miracle|KSV Miracle]] roster, due to restrictions from [[Blizzard]]. {{citation needed}} KSV would go on to win both the [[heroes:2017_Gold_Club_World_Championship|2017]] and [[heroes:2018_Heroes_of_the_Storm_Global_Championship/Phase_2/Finals|2018]] HOTS [[heroes:Heroes_of_the_Storm_Global_Championship|Global Championships]] before [[Blizzard]] ended HOTS esports in December of 2018. {{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2018/gaming/news/heroes-of-the-storm-esports-1203089770/|title=Blizzard Is Ending ‘Heroes of the Storm’ Esports Plans|date=2018-12-14|author=[[Emily Gera]]|publisher=[[Variety]]}} On November 7th, 2017, KSV announced its entrance into the [[pubg:Main Page|PUBG]] scene, with the team [[pubg:KSV AseL|KSV Asel]]. {{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/GenG/status/934974078951108608?s=20|title=Support our KSV PUBG Team(AseL)'s new start!|author=[[Gen.G Esports]]|date=2017-11-26}} Just 3 weeks later, on November 29th, 2017, KSV announced a second team for PUBG: [[pubg:KSV Notitle|KSV Notitle]].{{citation needed}} On August 16th, 2018, Gen.G announced the merging of the two teams.{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/Gen_G_esports/status/1029954770696425472|title=Regarding Gen.G PUBG roster change for PKL Season 2|author=[[Gen.G Esports]]|date=2018-08-16}} The resulting team has proved very succesful over the years, winning the first PUBG World Championship [[pubg:PUBG_Global_Invitational/2018|PUBG Global Invitational 2018]], the [[pubg:PUBG_Global_Championship/2019|2019 Global Championship]] and placing third at the [[pubg:PUBG_Global_Invitational.S/2021|2021 Global Invitational]]. The KSV [[:leagueoflegends:Gen.G|League of Legends team]] formed on November 30th, 2017, with the acquisition of the [[wikipedia:Samsung|Samsung]] Esports division, which included the 2017 World Champions [[:leagueoflegends:Samsung Galaxy|Samsung Galaxy]]. {{cite web |url=https://n.news.naver.com/mnews/article/144/0000525673 |title=롤드컵 우승팀 '삼성 갤럭시' KSV에 매각|author=조진호 |date=2017-12-01 |publisher=경향신문 |language={{FlagNoLink|kr}} Korean|trans_title=Worlds Winner 'Samsung Galaxy' Sold to KSV}} The team, now named Gen.G Esports, would qualify for the [[leagueoflegends:World_Championship/2018|2018 World Championships]] but would end up being knocked out promptly in the group stage, with a 1-5 record, in a year with a particularly bad showing from the South Korean teams. {{cite web|url=https://www.invenglobal.com/articles/9408/worlds-2019-highlights-and-takeaways-from-the-group-stage|title=[Worlds 2019] Highlights and Takeaways from the Group Stage|date=2019-10-20|author=[[Nick Geracie]]|publisher=[[InvenGlobal]]}} Due to missing out on the [[leagueoflegends:World_Championship/2019|2019 World Championships]], the team's next appearance on the world stage would be at the [[leagueoflegends:World_Championship/2020|2020 World Championships]]. Gen.G would make it till the quarter finals before being eliminated by [[G2 Esports]]. {{See also|leagueoflegends:Gen.G Esports#History|l1=History of Gen.G LoL Team}} With the announcement of [[rocketleague:Gen.G_Mobil1_Racing|Gen.G Mobil1 Racing]] and [[rocketleague:Gen.G_Mobil1_Racing_Black|Gen.G Mobil1 Racing Black]] on September 28th, 2022 Gen.G Esports enters the [[rocketleague:Main_Page|Rocket League]] scene. {{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/GenG/status/1575213757650898944|title=The moment you’ve all been waiting for|author=[[Gen.G Esports]]|date=2022-09-28}} Gen.G Mobil1 Racing entered the [[rocketleague:Rocket_League_Championship_Series/2022-23|RLCS 2022-23]] circuit with finishing Top 2 in all three North American Regionals of the Fall Split while winning the [[rocketleague:Rocket_League_Championship_Series/2022-23/Fall/North_America/Invitational|Fall Invitational]]. The team entered the [[rocketleague:Rocket_League_Championship_Series/2022-23/Fall|Fall Major]] as North America's first seed and ended up winning the whole tournament continuing their record of not finishing outside the Top 2 at RLCS Events. ====Game Timeline==== {{TeamTimeline |height=600|startYear=2017 |game1=overwatch |game1start= 2017-07-12|game1end= 2023-11-21|game1start2= 2024-12-28 |game2=heroes |game2start= 2017-11-05|game2end= 2018-12-21 |game3=leagueoflegends|game3start= 2017-11-30 |game4=pubg |game4start= 2018-08-16 |game5=clashroyale |game5start= 2018-08-16|game5end= 2019-11-04 |game6=fortnite |game6start= 2018-10-25|game6end= 2022-12-13 |game7=callofduty |game7start= 2019-01-31|game7end= 2019-12-02 |game8=apexlegends |game8start= 2019-03-01|game8end= 2019-11-19|game8start2= 2025-05-31 |game9=counterstrike |game9start= 2019-12-06|game9end= 2021-02-04|game9start2= 2024-02-21|game9end2=2024-10-21 |game10=valorant |game10start=2020-05-04 |game11=rocketleague |game11start=2022-09-28 |game12=honorofkings |game12start=2022-11-09|game12end=2022-12-10|game12start2=2025-01-11 |game13=easportsfc |game13start=2023-03-01|game13end=2023-11-26|game13start2=2024-01-18 |game14=pubgm |game14start=2024-01-23|game14end=2025-01-03|game14start2=2025-02-06|game14end2=2025-12-29 |game15=starcraft2 |game15start=2024-06-01|game15end=2024-12-01 |game16=brawlstars |game16start=2024-10-08|game16end=2025-12-31 |game17=chess |game17start=2025-02-05 |game18=halo |game18start=2025-04-10|game18end=2025-06-20 |game19=thefinals |game19start=2025-10-08|game19end=2025-12-15|game19start2=2026-02-04 |game20=trackmania |game20start=2026-02-04 |game21=deltaforce |game21start=2026-06-22 }} ===Corporate History=== Gen.G Esports was formed in 2017 as KSV eSports by [[Kevin Chou]] and [[Kent Wakeford]], co-founders of the video game development company [[wikipedia:Kabam|Kabam]]. The organization started out by acquiring the rights for an [[overwatch:Overwatch_League|Overwatch League]] franchise in Seoul, South Korea. The purchase reporterdly amounted to $20 million with the intention to hire both an all-Korean roster as well as an all-Korean management staff.{{cite web|url=https://venturebeat.com/2017/07/12/why-kabam-cofounder-kevin-chou-is-diving-into-esports-with-overwatch-leagues-seoul-franchise/|title=Why Kabam cofounder Kevin Chou is diving into esports with Overwatch League’s Seoul franchise|date=2017-07-12|author=[[Dean Takahashi]]|publisher=[[VentureBeat]]}} This team would later be known as the [[overwatch:Seoul Dynasty|Seoul Dynasty]]. '''Sentinels''' (formerly known as '''Phoenix1''' and often abbreviated as '''SEN''') is a professional esports organization owned by P1 Esports, LLC, and founded in May 2016. Sentinels currently has teams in six different games and formerly had a League of Legends squad. Sentinels also formerly held a minority stake in the [[overwatch:Los Angeles Gladiators|Los Angeles Gladiators]] of the [[overwatch:Overwatch League|Overwatch League]], which they operated from 2017 to 2019.

{{GameArticle}}

==Competitive History==
Phoenix1 debuted as a League of Legends squad in 2016, acquiring the spot of Team Impulse in [[leagueoflegends:LCS/North_America/2016/Summer|NA LCS Summer 2016]]. The team finished 8th, but survived the promotion tournament and returned to LCS the following spring. Phoenix1 took 3rd in NA LCS Spring 2017 and 9th in Summer 2017, again surviving the promotion tournament after the latter finish. After LCS went to a [[leagueoflegends:NA LCS Franchising|franchised model]] for the 2018 season, Phoenix1 was denied entry after applying for a franchise, ending their League of Legends division.

On June 6th, 2018, Phoenix1 rebranded to Sentinels and signed three [[hearthstone:Sentinels|Hearthstone]] players. A month later, Sentinels signed the roster of TT to begin their [[fortnite:Sentinels|Fortnite division]].

On March 25th, 2019, Sentinels signed [[fortnite:Bugha|Bugha]], a 16-year-old Fortnite player who would go on to win that year's [[fortnite:Fortnite World Cup/2019/Finals/Solo|Fortnite World Cup]] and {{Abbr/USD}}$3,000,000. On March 26th, Sentinels began their [[apexlegends:Sentinels|Apex Legends]] division.

On February 17th, 2020, Sentinels started a [[halo:Sentinels|Halo team]], which debuted the following week with a third place finish at [[halo:DreamHack_Halo_Series/2020/Anaheim|DreamHack Anaheim]]. Two months later, the organization began their [[valorant:Sentinels|VALORANT]] division.

In March 2021, Sentinels VALORANT defeated [[FaZe Clan]] to win [[valorant:VALORANT_Champions_Tour/2021/North_America/Stage_1/Masters|VCT North America Masters]], the first first-party NA major tournament. On May 30th, the team defeated [[Fnatic]] and won [[valorant:VALORANT_Champions_Tour/2021/Stage_2/Masters|Stage 2 Masters]], the first international VALORANT major, and {{Abbr/USD}}$200,000. On August 6th, Sentinels started a [[wildrift:Sentinels|Wild Rift team]].

On May 1st, 2022, Sentinels' Halo team won the [[halo:Halo_Championship_Series/2021-22/Kansas_City|HCS Kansas City Major]].

Following the [[100 Thieves]] sale of their franchise [[leagueoflegends:LCS|LCS]] slot, Sentinels rejoined League of Legends on October 10th, 2025. <ref name="senlcs">{{cite web|url=https://x.com/Sentinels/status/1976694532617212280|title=The next era of Sentinels|author=[[Sentinels]]|date=2025-10-10}}</ref>

==Corporate History==
===Early History===
Sentinels was founded as Phoenix1 on May 26th, 2016, by [[wikipedia:Paramount Pictures|Paramount Pictures]] Vice Chairman [[wikipedia:Rob Moore (executive)|Rob Moore]], film producer Jack Giarraputo, and Moore's son Michael.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/esports/story/_/id/15751788/phoenix1-replaces-team-impulse-picks-gate-mash-slooshi-more|title=Phoenix1 replaces Team Impulse, picks up Gate, Mash, Slooshi, and more|author=Tyler Erzberger|publisher=ESPN|date=2016-05-26}}</ref> In October 2017, following the announcement of NA LCS moving to a [[leagueoflegends:NA LCS Franchising|franchise model]], ESPN reported that Phoenix1 was one of two teams who had their franchise application denied by Riot Games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/esports/story/_/id/21045074/sources-phoenix1-team-envy-league-championship-series-franchise-applications-denied|title=Sources: Phoenix1 and Team Envy League Championship Series franchise applications denied|author=Jacob Wolf|publisher=ESPN|date=2017-10-16}}</ref> The following month, American entertainment company [[wikipedia:Kroenke Sports and Entertainment|Kroenke Sports and Entertainment]] (KSE) announced that their new [[overwatch:Overwatch League|Overwatch League]] franchise [[overwatch:Los Angeles Gladiators|Los Angeles Gladiators]] would be operated by Phoenix1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/esports/story/_/id/21264637/with-gladiators-announced-overwatch-league-all-twelve-teams-now-set|title=With the Gladiators announced for the Overwatch League, all twelve teams are now set|author=Imad Khan|publisher=ESPN|date=2017-11-02}}</ref>

On June 6th, 2018, Phoenix1 rebranded to Sentinels.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dotesports.com/business/news/phoenix1-rebrands-sentinels-24461|title=Former NA LCS organization Phoenix1 rebrands to Sentinels|author=Justin Binkowski|publisher=Dot Esports|date=2018-06-08}}</ref>

===Kroenke Sports & Entertainment lawsuit===
In August 2019, Sentinels CEO Rob Moore filed a lawsuit against KSE, alleging KSE purchased NA LCS team [[leagueoflegends:Echo Fox|Echo Fox]] without Sentinels' knowledge, which was "a violation of a verbal joint venture agreement" that allowed Sentinels to have complete control over KSE's esports operations<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/esports/story/_/id/27304848/sentinels-ceo-sues-kroenke-sports-entertainment-echo-fox-purchase|title=Sentinels CEO sues Kroenke Sports & Entertainment over Echo Fox purchase|author=Jacob Wolf|publisher=ESPN|date=2019-08-01}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.esportsobserver.com/sentinels-ceo-sues-kroenke/|title=Sentinels CEO Sues Kroenke Sports & Entertainment Over Echo Fox LCS Deal|author=Andrew Hayward|publisher=The Esports Observer|date=2019-08-02}}</ref> Moore sought for Sentinels to hold a 51% stake in the Gladiators joint venture in which they held 49% at the time. The lawsuit was settled after the Echo Fox acquisition fell through, with the parties mutually parting ways and KSE gaining full ownership of the Gladiators. KSE announced plans to create an esports team to oversee their Overwatch and [[callofduty:Los Angeles Guerrilas|Call of Duty]] operations (which came to be [[The Guard]]), while Sentinels announced plans to expand into other games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.esportsobserver.com/sentinels-split-kroenke-se/|title=Report: Kroenke Sports & Entertainment Splits with Sentinels for LA Gladiators Management|author=Andrew Hayward|publisher=The Esports Observer|date=2019-09-18}}</ref>

'''Talon Esports''' (also known simply as '''Talon''') is a professional esports organization founded in 2017 and headquartered in Hong Kong.

{{GameArticle}}

==Competitive History==
The organization was founded with the signing of Taiwan-based [[:overwatch:Royal Restricted Area|Royal Restricted Area]] as their [[:overwatch:Talon Esports|Overwatch squad]] in March 2017. After failing to qualify for Season 2 of the [[:overwatch:Overwatch Pacific Championship/2017/Season 2|Overwatch Pacific Championship]], the Overwatch team disbanded on July 23. In February 2018, Talon acquired the [[:overwatch:Overwatch Contenders|Overwatch Contenders]] slot of [[:overwatch:Ardeont|Ardeont]] to compete in 2018 Season 1. In December 2019, the team partnered  with [[:wikipedia:PSG Esports|Paris Saint-Germain Esports]] to form [[:leagueoflegends:PSG Talon|PSG Talon]] to compete in the first season of the League of Legends [[:leagueoflegends:PCS/2020/Spring|Pacific Championship Series]]. Talon also has teams in [[:fighters:Talon Esports|Street Fighter, Tekken 7]], [[:arenaofvalor:Talon Esports|Arena of Valor]], [[rainbowsix:Talon Esports|Rainbow Six]], and [[clashroyale:Talon Esports|Clash Royale]],  and formerly held a team in [[:pubg:Talon Esports|PUBG]].

{{Team achievements table}}

==Corporate History==
Talon was founded by Sean Zhang and Jarrod Tham with the signing of their Overwatch team on March 13, 2017. The team branched out to fighting games a few months later, which, after the release of their Overwatch team in July, left the players as Talon's only esports venture. In 2018, Talon added Arena of Valor and readded Overwatch, moving them back to a multi-game organization. 

On November 18th, 2019, New Wave Esports announced their investment in Talon, which also included a consulting agreement between the two companies.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.talon.gg/blogs/news/new-wave-esports-x-talon|title=NEW WAVE ESPORTS X TALON|date=2019-11-18|publisher=[[Talon Esports]]}}</ref> On June 18th, 2020, Talon announced a joint partnership with French esports team [[:wikipedia:PSG Esport|PSG Esports]], the gaming branch of Ligue 1 football team [[:wikipedia:Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]], to jointly own a League of Legends team to compete in the Pacific Championship Series known as PSG Talon; the team was a rebranding of the already-existing Talon Esports LoL team, which won the 2020 [[:leagueoflegends:PCS/2020/Spring|PCS Spring]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.talon.gg/blogs/news/talon-partners-with-psg|title=TALON PARTNERS WITH PSG|date=2020-06-18|publisher=[[Talon Esports]]}}</ref> On October 12th, Talon announced the completion of their seed funding round, in which they received {{Abbr/USD}}$2 million in investments.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.talon.gg/blogs/news/talon-raises-2m-for-apac|title=TALON RAISES $2M FOR APAC|date=2020-10-12|publisher=[[Talon Esports]]}}</ref>

In October 2020, Talon became the exclusive tournament operator for Southeast Asian [[:valorant:Main Page|VALORANT]] tournaments in 2020 and 2021, specifically professional tournaments in Hong Kong and Taiwan, as well as collegiate tournaments in Hong Kong. This deal began with [[:valorant:First Strike/Hong Kong and Taiwan|First Strike Hong Kong & Taiwan]] in December 2020, part of the first Riot Games-supported regional tournament series.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://esportsobserver.com/riot-games-sea-valorant-plans/|title=Riot Games Reveals Esports Plans for Valorant in the SEA Region; Announces Partnership with Seven Organizations|author=Shounak Sengupta|date=2020-10-14|publisher=The Esports Observer}}</ref>

In 2021, Talon announced a number of sponsorships, most notably KFC Thailand for its Arena of Valor team and Gigabyte Aorus for PSG Talon.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://esportsobserver.com/talon-kfc-thailand-rov/|title=Talon Esports Partners With KFC Thailand for Arena of Valor Team|author=James Fudge|date=2021-01-28|publisher=The Esports Observer}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://esportsobserver.com/psg-talon-auros-partner/|title=PSG Talon Partners With AORUS|author=James Fudge|date=2021-03-22|publisher=The Esports Observer}}</ref> On March 31st, Talon announced its debut merchandise series.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.talon.gg/blogs/news/talon-esports-launches-debut-merchandise-collection-for-spring-summer-2021|title=TALON ESPORTS LAUNCHES DEBUT MERCHANDISE COLLECTION FOR SPRING/SUMMER 2021|date=2021-03-31|publisher=[[Talon Esports]]}}</ref>

On January 5th, 2025, '''Talon Esports''' and '''[[Paris Saint-Germain Esports]]''' announce the end of their [[League of Legends]] partnership. <ref>{{cite web |url=https://x.com/talonesportslol/status/1875875582283743720|title=TALON and Paris Saint-Germain Esports: Conclusion of League of Legends Partnership|author=[[Talon Esports|TALON LOL]]|date=2025-01-05}}</ref>
